mainEntity.name: What is NAD+ and what does it do?

acceptedAnswer.text: NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is a coenzyme that plays a central role in cellular energy production and DNA repair. Levels naturally decline with age. Supplementation via IM or IV is intended to support mitochondrial function, energy and cognitive performance, particularly in longevity-focused wellness.

mainEntity.name: How does IM differ from IV NAD+?

acceptedAnswer.text: IM injection is faster and more practical for regular maintenance, with a slightly lower peak concentration. Full IV NAD+ delivers higher doses over a longer infusion, often used as a more intensive entry protocol. We recommend IM for most maintenance cases and IV when a deeper baseline reset is the goal.

Side effects are uncommon and usually mild — slight injection site discomfort, occasional transient warmth or chest pressure during full IV protocols. The IM route is generally very tolerable. We screen for contraindications and review medications before every NAD+ session.
